archetype.name: Lost Season (February collapse)
archetype.definition: A team that stayed within reach of .500 for three months, then lost every game in February and played out the rest of the year as one of the league's weaker sides, finishing with its worst record in five seasons.

report.headline: Near-.500 through January, then an 0-11 February buried the season

recap.finish: 31-51, fourth in the Central; missed the postseason
recap.body:
For three months this looked like the same Bulls team as the last few years: fast, three-happy, around .500 and stuck in the middle. A 5-0 October gave way to a 4-10 November, but December (7-7) and January (8-8) steadied things, and the team sat at 24-25 at the end of January. That was roughly the 39-43 pace of the two previous seasons, and the play-in race was still open.

February ended that. The Bulls went 0-11, the season's longest losing streak, while scoring only 106.73 a game and allowing 124. They never recovered. March went 5-10 and April 2-5. Over the final ten games they went 2-8 and allowed 126.8 a game, worse than their season norm. Both wins in that stretch came against Washington, and the losses included a 96-136 rout at New York and a 128-149 finale in Dallas. From 24-25, they finished 31-51.

The team was below average at both ends. Its ORtg of 113 ranked 23rd and its DRtg of 118.1 ranked 22nd, for a Net Rtg of -5.1, 22nd in the league. The shooting was fine: eFG % of 54.7 sat right at the league average on a high 44.3 3PA Rate. The offense lost ground on everything around the shot. It ranked 27th in ORB %, 22nd in FT Rate and 23rd in TOV %. The defense forced almost nothing, with an Opp TOV % of 11.1 that ranked 29th, and it let opponents shoot 36.8% from three. Playing at a 102.5 Pace, well above the league's, gave opponents more possessions to exploit those gaps.

The roster split cleanly. The guards carried it: Tre Jones (63.7 TS %, a team-best 5.7 Win Shares) and Josh Giddey (13th of 89 on the point-guard tab, 494 assists, 2.7 BPM) gave the backcourt its C+, the best grade on the team. The frontcourt graded F. Matas Buzelis played the most minutes and scored 1,252 points with 173 threes, but his BPM was -1. Patrick Williams played 1,474 minutes with a 49.4 TS %, -0.1 Win Shares and a -9.6 On-Off. The centers behind Jalen Smith were worse. Opposing power forwards and centers scored well above their own averages against Chicago.

Luck doesn't explain the record. A W vs Pt Diff of +2 means the margin implied 29 wins, so 31-51 slightly flatters a team that was outscored by 427 points. The step back from last year is real. Net Rtg fell from -1.5 to -5.1, and the defense slid from 115.6 to 118.1 DRtg, the drop accounting for most of the decline.

highlights.title: The guards held the offense up
highlights.body: Tre Jones was the most efficient regular on the roster, and Giddey was a genuine top-15 point guard by the site's rankings, filling the box score with 448 rebounds and 494 assists. Their play is why the backcourt graded C+ while the rest of the roster lagged. Both are established producers rather than hot streaks, so this is the group to build from.

highlights.title: Buzelis took on a full load
highlights.body: Buzelis led the team in minutes, points and threes and ranked 29th of 93 on the power-forward tab, with a 58.6 TS % on 22.8 USG %. His BPM (-1) and On-Off (-1.9) show he wasn't yet winning his minutes. Still, he carried that volume efficiently, which is the hard part.

highlights.title: Defensive glass was a real strength
highlights.body: Chicago grabbed 75.5% of opponents' misses, sixth in the league and above the league's 74. It was one of the few things this defense did well. It mattered because the team rarely forced turnovers, so ending possessions on the boards was its main way of getting stops.

lowlights.title: An 0-11 February ended the year
lowlights.body: The team went into February at 24-25 and came out at 24-36. The offense fell to 106.73 a game in that month, far below anything it managed in any other month. The sheet doesn't say who was missing, but the team never got back to its early-season level: March and April were both losing months, and the last ten games were worse defensively than the season as a whole.

lowlights.title: A failing-grade frontcourt
lowlights.body: The frontcourt graded F. Patrick Williams, Guerschon Yabusele and Nick Richards all posted negative BPMs and steep negative On-Offs in heavy minutes. Opposing power forwards and centers scored more than their own averages, ranking among the worst in the league in that split. Jalen Smith's +12.4 On-Off in only 1,095 minutes suggests this group can be fixed with personnel, not just better luck.

lowlights.title: A defense that forced nothing
lowlights.body: Opponents turned it over on 11.1% of plays, 29th in the league. That echoes last year's 10.8, so it is a lasting trait of this group rather than a one-year slump. Without turnovers, the defense relied on opponents missing shots, and they mostly didn't: opponents shot 36.8% from three, 23rd, and the DRtg landed 22nd.

arc.note: A 5-0 start and a near-.500 record through January gave way to an 0-11 February, and the team never climbed back, finishing 2-8 over its last ten games.

recap.nextYear:
Not much of this year was bad luck. The margin implied 29 wins and the team won 31, so the record is an honest one. The core of the decline is the defense, which got worse after an already middling year, and the frontcourt, which graded F. Too many minutes went to bigs with negative BPMs and On-Offs, while Jalen Smith, the one big whose minutes clearly helped, played the fewest of the regular bigs. The backcourt is the foundation. Jones and Giddey produced at a level worth keeping, though Sexton's points came with a -6.6 On-Off and Okoro's minutes graded poorly. Buzelis is the volume piece whose impact numbers need to catch up. The shooting profile is league-average and the pace is a choice, so the improvement has to come from forcing turnovers, protecting the ball, crashing the offensive glass and finding a frontcourt that can hold its matchups.

The wings graded C, but the sheet lists almost no wing minutes beyond Leonard Miller, so that group is close to a blank slate as well.

Put simply, the work for next season sits up front and on defense; the guards are not the problem.
